newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech bank approves capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Czech bank approves capital increase.

text.p: Czech Banka Hana a.s., partly-owned by Belgium's Kredietbank NV, said on Monday its shareholders had approved a 500 million crown increase in its basic capital, through a share rights issue.
A Banka Hana statement said the issue, if successful, would raise its basic capital to two billion crowns by the end of the year.
It said that current shareholders would have the right to subscribe to the issue between November 6-19. The issue would then be open to the public between November 26-December 3.
The statement did not give any further details of the issue.

The statement said that reasons for the increase included "encourage an environment for further trading activies of the bank and allowing the bank to meet the capital adequacy requirements as set out by the central bank".
The statement also said the issue would help the solvency and liquidity of the bank in "such a competitive environment".
"(The increase) creates space so that strategic partners can further raise their stake," the statement said.
The local news agency CTk reported in late August that Kredietbank had increased its stake in Banka Hana to above 10 percent, though it did not give an exact figure.
